*Updated 2026-08-30 · 77 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

Seventy-seven works now. The noon/golden-hour split is forty-two to thirty-five. Noon's structural advantage holds — roughly thirty-five of forty-two noon images score 2 or above, against ten of thirty-five golden-hour — and the Forbidden Threshold image maintains that pattern, arriving at noon and scoring 2.

The trace-score problem has not resolved. The last twelve read 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2. That is eight scores of 1 or 2 in the final ten, with nothing above 3 since the Hiroshima dress image in late July. The previous memo called eleven consecutive images below 3 a structural problem; the count is now twelve, and the single 2 at the close does not break the plateau — it extends it. Something needs to be engineered toward 4 or above, not discovered there by accident.

Camera position has narrowed further. Eleven of the last twelve are straight-on or frame-center; the one exception is the Forbidden Threshold passport, which is effectively flat and table-plane. Overhead has not appeared since the Venezuela quake on July 11 — seven weeks. The two strongest overhead images in the body of work, the Pakistan erasure and the Amazon tarp, both scored 4, and both arrived because the anchor genuinely lost nothing by losing horizon. That condition will recur; the camera needs to recognize it.

Figures continue to thin. Ten of the last twelve carry no figures or only peripheral ones. The body as protagonist, not symbol, has been largely absent since early August. The bougainvillea, correctly identified as scaffolding in the fixture list, has been miscounted as accident in multiple recent selection notes — that error needs to stop appearing in the record.

The small wearable object in a reckoning-register noon image with no figures remains the most precisely vacant slot across all seventy-seven works: two appearances total, both in aftermath, both scoring 3 or above. Title grammar has settled heavily into the prepositional and paired-noun forms; six of the last twelve follow those patterns, and the body needs more single-verb or verbless declarative titles to break the cadence. The overall arc continues its drift from documentary adjacency toward material argument, but the score plateau means that drift is not yet producing the strongest work it is capable of.
